title: Text-to-CAD Evaluation with CADTests
claim: Executable tests judge generated outputs by whether they satisfy the specification, not by similarity to a single reference, handling ambiguity and subtle errors.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, top-to-bottom flow, green pass vs pink fail boxes
description: Two columns show the same top-to-bottom flow: a text Prompt, then 3D renderings of a Generated B-Rep (brownish-red) next to a Reference B-Rep (gray), then a CADTest Description box, then a CADTest Execution result. On the left, the generated model, a trough-shaped prism, differs from the reference but satisfies the prompt. Two green dashed test boxes lead to 'Passed All Tests: True'. On the right, a block with a hole and slit looks close to the reference. Red-outlined zoom insets with hand-pointer icons highlight a slit that is not cut all the way through. A pink test box shows the failure message (expected 16 vertices, found 18) and leads to 'Passed All Tests: False'. Italic captions below each column state the takeaway. The eye goes first to the colored 3D models, then to the green and pink result boxes.
caption: CADTests are executable programs that verify prompt specifications directly on the generated geometry. CADTests can account for ambiguous design prompts (left) and identify subtle structural errors (right). The figure ommits CADTest implementations for clarity.
abstract: Text-to-CAD has recently emerged as an important task with the potential to substantially accelerate design workflows. Despite its significance, there has been surprisingly little work on Text-to-CAD evaluation, and assessing CAD model generation performance remains a considerable challenge. In this work, we introduce a new evaluation perspective for Text-to-CAD based on automated testing. We propose CADTestBench, the first test-based benchmark for Text-to-CAD, based on CADTests, executable software tests that verify whether a generated CAD model satisfies the geometric and topological requirements of the input prompt. Using CADTestBench, we conduct comprehensive benchmarking of recent Text-to-CAD methods and further demonstrate that CADTests can also guide CAD model generation, yielding simple baselines that surpass performance of current methods. CADTestBench code and data are available.
